title: A Phone Call, a Newspaper Advert and Sabin's First Room in Brasília
dek: In 1984 two biochemists put their savings into a closed laboratory's equipment and opened Laboratório Sabin in a 90-square-metre room in Brasília.

story.founder: Janete Vaz and Sandra Soares Costa
story.event: Two biochemists opening a clinical laboratory in Brasília with secondhand equipment
story.summary: On 2 May 1984 the biochemists Janete Vaz and Sandra Soares Costa opened Laboratório Sabin in a 90-square-metre room in Brasília's Asa Norte, with three employees and equipment bought from a newspaper advertisement with a US$4,000 deposit and instalments. In a field run mostly by influential men, they competed on service; a health-plan agreement soon covered basic costs. By 2011 its management system was built on ISO 9001 and the PALC accreditation programme, with external audits, and in 2020 it was reported accredited by the College of American Pathologists.
paragraphs: Laboratório Sabin opened in Brasília on 2 May 1984, and it began with a telephone call. Sandra Soares Costa, a biochemist from Inhapim in Minas Gerais, rang her friend Janete Vaz to ask whether Vaz's idea of setting up a laboratory together still stood. The two had met while working at a private laboratory in the city. On the Saturday morning that Costa accepted, Vaz later recalled, they went straight out to look for a room.

Vaz had grown up on a farm near Anápolis, trained in pharmacy and biochemistry at the Federal University of Goiás, and held a public post at the Hospital Regional de Taguatinga; at one point she worked three jobs at once. Clinical laboratories in the capital were then run mostly by men, often doctors and university professors with influence. Neither partner fitted that description, so they chose to compete on service: careful attention to patients, mobile collection points and, Costa later said, a readiness to use computers when much of the market resisted them.

After walking Asa Sul and Asa Norte, they chose a 90-square-metre room in the Edifício de Clínicas, close to the Asa Norte regional hospital and the bus station, so that anyone could get there. Sitting on the pavement outside, they began planning what equipment to buy, then saw an advertisement in the Correio Braziliense offering a complete laboratory's equipment. They put down all they had saved, US$4,000, and paid the rest in instalments: six in one account Vaz gave, ten in another. They opened with three employees and did everything themselves, from collecting samples to keeping the books. A few months in, an agreement with a health plan began to cover the basic bills.

Vaz later called the first fifteen years very hard. In 2000 the laboratory moved into the Brasília Shopping complex and the partners set out to earn formal certifications. By 2011 its management system was built on ISO 9001 and on PALC, the clinical laboratory accreditation programme of the Brazilian Society of Clinical Pathology, with regular external audits. In February 2020, after an audit by five international assessors the previous November, Sabin was reported accredited by the College of American Pathologists.

quote.text: the logarithmic tables to be corrected, for by the error of some calculator the vessel often splits upon a rock that should have reached a friendly pier
quote.source_title: Walden, and On The Duty Of Civil Disobedience, Project Gutenberg eBook #205
quote.connection: Thoreau, half mocking the merchant's life, names the part of any trade that never ends: correcting the tables that others steer by. A laboratory's results are such tables. Sabin's later certifications are a record of that correcting, done again and again, long after the first room in Asa Norte.

reflection: A laboratory with ISO 9001, PALC and CAP behind it can make you forget that it once had three staff, secondhand equipment and two founders who also kept the accounts. Sabin's certifications came years after that first room. What the founders talk about from those early years is service: reaching patients, getting results out.

Most laboratories talQen hopes to serve will look more like that room than like Sabin today. That is worth keeping in view as you design. The tables need correcting every morning, often by people already doing three jobs, and something that helps on a short-staffed Tuesday may matter more than anything that only pays off at the next audit.
invitation: Today, ask one colleague what they would check first if they ran a laboratory of three people with no accreditation yet. Write their answer down before the day gets busy.

cross_checks.claim: Laboratório Sabin was founded in Brasília in May 1984 (2 May) by the biochemists Janete Vaz and Sandra Soares Costa
It opened in a 90 m² room with three employees
The founders bought a complete set of laboratory equipment and paid for it with a deposit and instalments
The laboratory field in Brasília was then dominated by influential men, doctors and university professors
The founders met while working at a private laboratory in Brasília

research_notes: Founders' interviews are in Portuguese and are paraphrased, not quoted. Two of the richest founder sources are sponsored: the Correio Braziliense 2022 piece sits under 'Parceiros: Sabin' (partner content) and the InfoMoney piece is MoneyLab content for XP Investimentos; both are cited for the founders' own recollections, which the story attributes ('Vaz later recalled', 'in one account Vaz gave'), and the dates and staff numbers are checked against the company's 2011 report and independent trade press. Instalments: six in the Correio 2022 account, ten in the InfoMoney account; both are given. The equipment came, in one account, from an advertisement for a complete laboratory's equipment, and in the other from a laboratory that had closed; these are compatible, and the story describes only the advertisement. Opening staff: three (Sabin's 2011 report, Saúde Business 2012, Correio 2022 and 2025) against four (NSC Total 2025 and a sponsored Metrópoles feature, not cited); the story uses three. Location: Correio 2022 quotes Vaz choosing the Edifício de Clínicas in Asa Norte near HRAN, and the 2011 report still lists a unit there; a Nosso Meio profile (not cited) places the first room next to the Hospital Regional de Taguatinga, where Vaz had worked, which looks like a conflation; the story follows the founders' own account. Vaz's move to Brasília is dated 1981 by InfoMoney and 'at 23' (about 1977-78) by Nosso Meio, so no year is given. Accreditation: the 2011 report lists ISO 9001:2008, ISO 14001:2004 and PALC; 'PALC: 2010' there is the version of the standard, not the year of first accreditation, which the sources reviewed do not give; the report describes the system as based on these standards with systematic external audits by accrediting bodies (and a PALC audit in October 2011) without using the word 'certified' for ISO 9001, so the story says the system was 'built on' them 'by 2011'. Medicina S/A (2020) refers to Sabin's 'current accreditations PALC, PADI and ISO'. CAP: Medicina S/A, published 19 February 2020, reports the accreditation after a November audit (so November 2019) and quotes the technical director saying preparation began in 2017. The SA 8000 certification Vaz mentions is not dated in the sources and is not used. NSC Total says Sabin was named after Albert Sabin; no second source was found, so this is left out. Sabin's own website pages and the direct PDF links now redirect to an error page; the 2011 report is cited from the Internet Archive. Thoreau's passage lists, half ironically, the labours of a merchant's business; it is applied by analogy to a laboratory's results.
